body:
I would personally not bother with this method. You've already got `friend` access, so you might as well just `push_back` to the collection directly.

Alternatively, I guess you can also make this method public instead and drop the `friend` access.

This seems unfortunate to store in the actual serialized `Animation` resource, since it would then have an actual runtime impact as well. Just removing this and the corresponding `_set` and `_get` code seems to function just as well, with the caveat that the collapsed state isn't preserved when closing the scene/editor, which seems fine.

I guess this could be a viable candidate for `EditorSettings::set_project_metadata`, but I'm not seeing any resource-specific data being stored in there, so maybe not?
Why does this need to exist if we already have this state in `Animation::collapsed_groups`?

This part was coded before I added the collapse icon, with the idea just being that you could click on the left side of the control to expand/collapse it (and the icon would be added later). I could try using a more accurate hitbox with the same dimensions and position as the chevron icon itself, but I expect that would harm usability. The actual icon is pretty small, and there's not anything else right next to it, so being able to click in that general area and activate the collapsing behavior (what the user very likely wants to do) is helpful in practice. In this screenshot here, the green box is the clickable area that toggles the collapse behavior, and the red box is around the actual icon. I'm worried that would make it a much smaller target that users would need to really aim for, versus a general area they can click in to get the behavior they want.

As mentioned in the main thread comment, this was a concern I also had and discussed with people in RocketChat. We agreed it'd be best to use the same strategy as the scene tree node collapsing, so I'll be looking into that today 😄

Good question; I liked the idea of keeping this sort of state information stored locally, but it is undeniably a level of data duplication. I'll look at removing it so that there's just one source of truth for this info.
That's a very good point. For now I'll probably take the `friend` approach, but if necessary I can use public methods instead.

We're not suggesting you shrink the box. It's great as-is. We were just remarking on the variable name, which was a bit hard to understand at first. I don't personally think it's weird to call it `collapse_icon_rect` while still having it be sized the way you did.

It's very nitpicky though, so do as you wish.

Ah okay, sorry about the misunderstanding then! I agree that the name is a bit vague for its purpose, so I might rename it to something like `collapse_area_rect` (indicating it does not represent the precise area of the icon itself, but the area where you can click to run the collapse behavior).

What's the motivation behind calling `ProjectSettings::localize_path` everywhere? I would have thought that `Resource::get_path` would return a localized path.
Is calling this `groups_folded` maybe too generic, seeing as how it's specific to the `Animation` part of the resource? Maybe `animation_node_groups_folded` is more appropriate?
Same thing here about mixing "collapsed" and "folded" terminology.

It was quite a while ago now so I don't remember for certain, but I *think* it had to do with me being worried about special characters ending up in the filepath that would result in Godot not being able to save or load them correctly. I'll give it a try with just `Resource::get_path` and see if that works.
It seemed to work fine with just `get_path()`, so I removed the calls to `localize_path()` 🙂
I'd say this needs an explanation, using height for both looks odd without it

I agree, it does seem rather arbitrary. For now I've reworked it a bit to use the width of the left margin plus the width of the icon. I'm a little worried that this means the clickable area *might* change when the row is folded versus unfolded, but I tried toggling it a bit and it felt natural to me.
This should also be TOOLSE_ENABLED.
